candidates.description: A farm of real iPhones, run from your Mac. Open-source iOS device automation with live control, a Postgres-backed scheduler, and TikTok workflows. Self-hosted, Apache-2.0. Built at Agniverse, by An Nayal.
candidates.readme_excerpt:
# Phone Farm iOS

> Built at [Agniverse](https://agniverse.co), by [An Nayal](https://annayal.com) · used at [Handler](https://gethandler.ai) · more free tools at [annayal.com/open-source](https://annayal.com/open-source)

An open-source, standalone application for operating physical iOS devices and running scheduled TikTok workflows. It includes guided device registration, WDA/Appium supervision, live video and remote input, PostgreSQL-backed scheduling, recurring jobs, uploads, execution history, the dashboard/API server, and a built-in TikTok automation plugin.

It runs locally as-is; authentication is optional on a loopback bind. Harden it for a shared or exposed deployment by supplying your own `AuthProvider` (`PHONE_FARM_AUTH_PLUGIN`) and process supervision — no fork required. Tasks are persisted as `pluginId`, `taskType`, `taskVersion`, and a JSON payload, so an old schedule can never silently execute a new contract.

> Live demo and setup walkthrough: **[gethandler.ai/ios-farm](https://gethandler.ai/ios-farm)**
>
> The full engineering writeup, TikTok on 9 real iPhones reverse engineered from the screen up (Apple's test daemon, the two WebDriverAgent patches, pixel-level UI detection, OCR account switching, never posting twice): **[gethandler.ai/tiktok-iphone-farm](https://gethandler.ai/tiktok-iphone-farm)**

## Documentation

- [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md) — install, configure, run, register a device
- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) — the four processes, data stores, task model, source map
- [docs/plugins.md](docs/plugins.md) — write a plugin: tasks, execution context, versioning, panels, routes
- [docs/coordinates.md](docs/coordinates.md) — tap-layout profiles and how to add one
- [PLUGIN_DEVELOPMENT.md](PLUGIN_DEVELOPMENT.md) — plugin trust and compatibility rules
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) — before exposing the dashboard beyond loopback

## Run the standalone application

Requirements are Node 22+, PostgreSQL, Xcode, a signed real-device WebDriverAgent, and Appium's XCUITest driver.

```sh
npm install
cp .env.example .env
npm run appium:install-driver
npm run db:up
npm run db:migrate
npm run wda:prepare
```

Run these long-lived processes (wrap each in a `launchd` agent or systemd unit for an always-on host):

```sh
npm run appium
npm run wda:service
npm run worker
npm run web
```

TikTok support is enabled by default. Set `PHONE_FARM_PLUGINS` to comma-separated ESM package names to add more task plugins.

# sprite-stacking

An agent skill that turns four pixel art views into fake-3D sprites you can spin. By Daniel White.

![MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-MIT-111?style=flat-square)
![Agent skill](https://img.shields.io/badge/agent-skill-111?style=flat-square)
![Python 3 + Pillow + NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python%203-Pillow%20%2B%20NumPy-111?style=flat-square)
![Works with](https://img.shields.io/badge/works%20with-Claude%20Code%20%C2%B7%20Codex%20%C2%B7%20Cursor%20%C2%B7%20OpenCode%20%C2%B7%20Gemini%20CLI%20%C2%B7%20Pi-111?style=flat-square)

![Six sprite-stacked assets spinning](media/showcase.gif)

## Install

```bash
npx skills add danielwh2/sprite-stacking
```

Installs to the current project. Add `-g` for every project, `-a claude-code` (or `codex`, `cursor`, ...) to pick an agent. Uses the [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills), Node 22.20 or later.

Or copy `skills/sprite-stacking` into your agent's skills folder:

| Agent | Folder |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/` |
| Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Pi | `~/.agents/skills/` |

## Use

Ask your agent:

- "Make a rotatable pixel art car."
- "Sprite stack this 4-view sheet and give me a turntable."
- "Add a fake 3D pixel art tree to my Godot game."

No image generator? The agent draws the views itself in a short Python script.

## How it works

![Sheet to slices to render](media/pipeline.png)

1. **Views:** top, side, front and back, orthographic, one row.
2. **Carve:** a voxel survives only where all four views cover it.
3. **Slices:** the volume is cut into a strip of flat layers, ground first.
4. **Render:** each layer is rotated, squashed for pitch and lifted 1 px.

## Slicer CLI

```bash
python3 skills/sprite-stacking/scripts/views_to_slices.py views.png slices.png \
  --slices 36 --preview check.png --html viewer.html
```

- `--slices N`: layer count. 15-20 chunky, 32-48 detailed.
- `--order reading`: force TOP, SIDE, FRONT, BACK. Default matches views by proportion.
- `--round`: towers, balloons, pots carve round, not square.
- `--side-nose right`: the side view faces right.
- `--colours N`: shared palette size, `0` keeps every colour.
- `--normals path.png`: save a matching 3D normal-map slice strip.
- `--emissive path.png`: save an auto-detected emissive mask strip (headlights, windows, neon).

## Viewer

`--html` writes a standalone page:
- **Modes:** Turntable, **Scene** (Living Diorama with **Neon Street** and **Meadow Island** proced

# NestJS agent skills

Official [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) for building and extending [NestJS](https://nestjs.com) applications with coding agents. They give an agent what its training data lacks:
- the current APIs, which are often newer than the model;
- Nest's first-party packages;
- the mistakes that still pass tests: a sign-in that leaks which emails exist, `@IsOptional()` letting `null` through to a 500, a rate limiter that never sees the user, an event stream that outlives a revoked key, and many more.

Each skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` that holds its rules, plus `references/` with longer recipes. Every recipe was run on the released packages. The skills work with any agent that reads the Agent Skills format: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others.

## Skills

| Skill | Use when |
| --- | --- |
| `nestjs` | creating or extending a NestJS application: starting a project, layout, module system, where the docs are, common mistakes |
| `nestjs-feature` | adding or changing endpoints: where code goes, modules and providers, validation (Zod with `@Body({ schema })` or class-validator), status codes, errors, HTTP options, Server-Sent Events |
| `nestjs-auth` | adding or changing authentication or authorization: `@nestjs/authentication` (passwords, sessions, tokens, API keys) and `@nestjs/authorization` (policies) |
| `nestjs-data` | adding or changing persistence: `@nestjs/drizzle` and `@nestjs/typeorm`, migrations, safe updates, paging, transactions |
| `nestjs-testing` | writing, running or fixing tests: unit, service and end-to-end tests, overriding providers and global guards, signing test users in |
| `nestjs-production` | preparing for production: configuration, logs, observability with NestJS Observe, health checks, rate limiting, OpenAPI, shutdown, deployment |

Agents load a skill when its description matches the task, so there's nothing to invoke by hand.

## Install

The skills live in [`skills/`](skills). Install them for one project (committed with the code, so everyone on the team gets them) or for your user account (every project on your machine).

[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1156626270772269217?logo=discord&style=for-the-badge)](https://discord.gg/JzTFvyjG6R)
[![BlueSky](https://img.shields.io/badge/@langchain4j-follow-blue?logo=bluesky&style=for-the-badge)](https://bsky.app/profile/langchain4j.dev)
[![X](https://img.shields.io/badge/@langchain4j-follow-blue?logo=x&style=for-the-badge)](https://x.com/langchain4j)
[![Maven Version](https://img.shields.io/maven-central/v/dev.langchain4j/langchain4j?logo=apachemaven&style=for-the-badge)](https://search.maven.org/#search|gav|1|g:"dev.langchain4j"%20AND%20a:"langchain4j")


## Introduction

Welcome!

The goal of LangChain4j is to simplify integrating LLMs into Java applications.

Here's how:
1. **Unified APIs:**
   LLM providers (like OpenAI or Google Vertex AI) and embedding (vector) stores (such as Pinecone or Milvus)
   use proprietary APIs. LangChain4j offers a unified API to avoid the need for learning and implementing specific APIs for each of them.

candidates.readme_excerpt: # open-slide The slide framework built for agents. Describe a deck, and your coding agent writes it as React. open-slide handles the canvas, scaling, navigation, hot reload, editing, and present mode. Every page is a React component rendered on a fixed 1920 × 1080 canvas. ```bash npx @open-slide/cli init my-deck cd my-deck npm run dev ``` [Documentation](https://open-slide.dev/docs) · [Changelog](https://open-slide.dev/changelog) ## Agent panel Connect the Claude Code or Codex CLI you already use and drive it from the browser. Press `A` on any slide to open the panel. ![The agent panel beside the canvas while Claude Code edits the open deck](.github/assets/agent-panel.webp) - **Draft a deck.** Click New deck on the home page and describe it. The agent writes it page by page while the canvas follows along. - **Edit what you see.** The current slide, page, and selected element go along with every message, so "make this bigger" just works. - **Apply comments** with one click from the comment bar. - **Uses your existing login.** The SDK installs into the workspace the first time you open the panel. No API keys to configure. Prefer the terminal? The bundled skills (`/create-slide`, `/apply-comments`, `/create-theme`) work with any coding agent, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others. ## Comment mode Press `C`, click an element or drag across a region, and leave a note. Notes are saved as `@slide-comment` markers in the source, and the agent applies them all in one pass. ![Comment mode with pinned notes beside the slide](.github/assets/comment-mode.webp) ## Present mode Fullscreen playback with keyboard navigation, and a presenter view with the next slide, speaker notes, and a timer. ![Presenter view with the current slide, next slide, speaker notes, and timer](.github/assets/presenter.webp) ## Also included - Visual editor with drag, resize, alignment guides, and inline text editing - Themes, page transitions, step-by-step reveals, and shared-element morphs - Assets manager with brand logo search via [svgl](https://svgl.app) and Google Fonts - Export to static HTML, PDF, and PPTX - Static build that deploys to Vercel, Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, or any static host ## Repository | Path | Description | | --- | --- | | [`packages/core`](packages/core) | `@open-slide/core`: runtime, Vite plugin, and th
